device.metaphor: a rowing boat on night water; every trade drills a hole, water jets in, the trader bails, corks plug the holes
device.opening: the trader standing in the boat, a drill punches the first hole with a burst
device.palette: ice white and blue on blue-black, red holes, cork tan
device.hud: trades today and fees paid, counting up with the holes, green when the plan is back

scenes.vo: Your boat has holes. Every trade you take drills one more hole in it.
Twenty trades a day felt busy and smart, but every single one cost a spread and a fee, and the water kept coming in.
You can bail as fast as you like, but with twenty holes the water always wins, and bailing can't keep up.
So plug the holes. Three good trades a day, each one planned, each one with a reason, and watch the water drain.
Fewer trades, more boat under you.
